Yes, when you run `pyenv virtualenv-delete <venv-name>`, **all packages installed in that virtual environment will be deleted** along with the environment itself.

This command completely removes the virtual environment directory, which includes:
- The Python interpreter copy
- All installed packages (pip packages)
- Any scripts or binaries in the environment
- The entire virtual environment folder

Essentially, it deletes everything associated with that specific virtual environment, giving you a clean slate. The packages are only installed within that virtual environment's directory structure, so when the directory is removed, they go with it.

If you need to preserve a list of packages before deletion, you can save them first:
```bash
# Save package list before deleting
pyenv activate <venv-name>
pip freeze > requirements.txt
pyenv deactivate

# Then delete
pyenv virtualenv-delete <venv-name>
```

This way you can recreate the environment with the same packages later if needed using `pip install -r requirements.txt`.
